observations: Photo 0 shows multiple large black plastic water tanks stacked in a yard.
The tanks have horizontal ribbing for structural support.
One tank in the background has a white logo with a spade symbol and the word 'GEEPEE' printed below it.
The tanks appear used, with visible dirt, stains, and some surface wear.
The ground is unpaved and dusty, suggesting an outdoor storage or sales area.
No capacity markings (e.g., 1000L) are visible on any tank in the photo.
The tanks are cylindrical with domed tops and appear to be standard household or commercial water storage units.

claims.evidence: The brand 'Geepee' is visible on the tank in photo 0, but the capacity '1000 Liters' is not visible on the tank or in any text. No label or marking confirms the volume.

claims.claim: Food grade, used only once for clean water. No crack, no leak, lids complete.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The tank may not be 1000 liters as claimed.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the tank's capacity label or a side view showing the volume marking.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a smaller or unknown capacity tank, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The tank may have structural damage or cracks not visible in the photo.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the tank's surface, especially around the base, seams, and top, showing any cracks, warping, or thinning.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially damaged, which reduces value.

risks.risk: The tank may not be food-grade or may have been previously used for non-potable water.
risks.proof: A photo of the tank's interior or a certificate of food-grade certification.
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-food-grade, which reduces value.

proof_requests: Close-up of the rating plate on the tank showing the brand and model.
A clear photo of the capacity label or marking on the tank.
A close-up photo of the tank's interior or base to check for cracks or damage.
A photo of any certification or label confirming food-grade status.
response.reason: What the item is shows, but not the model that sets its price: no photo shows it clearly enough to read. The shot asked for first would settle it.
